body: Keerimalai is a breathtakingly beautiful and serene lagoon located on the northern coast of Sri Lanka. It's a natural swimming pool surrounded by lush green hills, crystal clear waters, and an atmosphere that is both peaceful and energizing. Visitors flock to Keerimalai to take a dip in its healing waters, believed to have curative properties, and to bask in the tranquility of this idyllic spot. With its stunning natural beauty, rich history, and spiritual significance, Keerimalai is truly a hidden gem waiting to be discovered.
title: Discovering the Magic of Keerimalai: An Oasis of Tranquility in the Heart of Sri Lanka

body: The Keeramalai pond, located next to the sea, separated only by the surrounding wall, gets its fresh water from an underground freshwater spring. I tasted the water and found it slightly salty. People believe that this freshwater spring is connected through a tunnel to the Nilvarai Bottomless Well located about 10 kilometres away. There is no charge for bathing in the pond. However, it costs Rs 30 to use the changing rooms with lockers.Although TripAdvisor lists this as "hot springs", the water is not even warm! I shall submit a modification to this heading to reflect that this is a "fresh water" pond as opposed to "hot"! There are two ponds here, the larger one for males and the smaller one for females. There are separate changing rooms too for male and female visitors. Visitors are not permitted to use soap within ponds to prevent pollution. The miraculous powers associated with its waters are believed to cure skin infections and help childless women achieve pregnancy. Water analysis has confirmed the presence of high mineral content in the waters. There is a large decorated hall in front meant for visitors to rest. According to legend as narrated by our guide, an Indian princess born with a deformed face begot a human pretty face after bathing in this pond! Personally speaking, I refrained from having a bath, as it is to me a public bathing place with no chlorination! However, there were many people enjoying its waters quite happily!!
title: Water from Underground Spring - but not HOT.

body: I thought it was hot springs but when asked local people about it, they said it is considered as divine water and NOT hot springs. There are two ponds with steps. You are not allowed to wear sandals in to the pond and using soap and shampoo is prohibited.On the full moon and first moon days the nearby sea water mix with the fresh water in the pond and it becomes salty. The other days it is filled with fresh water. On the left side corner is the place the fresh water to flow in to the pond. First go to the sea and have some fun over there. (Also you can walk through the small canal to the sea that connects the pond through the water gate.).Then come to the pond and bath. No tickets. If you want to shower in fresh water pay Rs 30 and bath in the reserved place. You can visit the nearby temples.

According to the local, underground tunnel between the pool and the well was naturally formed, and have existed for over 500 years. The local also believe that by soaking in the pool can cure sickness.They seperate the female and male pools. Male pool are much bigger and can be viewed from outside; female pool is covered with tall walls and so it is totally private. When I visited, the female pool was empty.It is free to swim in the pool, but 30 rupees for bathing. No shampoo and shoes are allowed in the pools.I went there early morning at 9am, and was luckily to have a well spoken and friendly lady to show me around the pool. I tested the water, it was considerable warm.The water is clear, but there were some visible rubbish under the pool. There were also many small fishes in the pool. title: Underwhelming

body: Not sure where the name comes from. This is basically a bathing area that is fed by the sea water. They separate the bathing areas for men and women, with the bathing area for the women being enclosed by a tall wall. Its interesting, but I was actually expecting hot springs so this was a bit of a letdown. The water was clean, refreshing, and great on a warm day. But in the women's bathing area there are kids, and the sound of their screaming and laughing was bouncing off the walls and made it rather unpleasant.
title: These are not hot springs!

body: Nothing special really, but:- There is no much you can do nearby Jaffna- A tour to springs is interesting in itself as you explore the peninsula on the way and see how its changing after the civil war- If coupled with a few places in the area makes an interesting day trip- Definitely non-touristy - mostly locals there, so that is quite nice, you get an opportunity to have a glimpse of real Sri Lanka
title: Not breathtaking but quite interesting

body: Mens' bath is interesting, but the ladies' was said to be good. The photo exhibition in the hall nearby is worth a look.
title: Worth the effort

body: Actually getting there was half the fun. The trip takes us to the country side and exposed us to the rural side of Jaffna. The temple complex is right by the ocean and presented an interesting combination of old and new Hindu temples. There were many young man enjoying the swim on the men’s pool, but not a single woman on their side. This is a recommend trip to get a feel for what the most northern end of Sri Lanka is like.
title: Swimming in a spring by the ocean

body: I'd planned on taking a dip in the springs, which aren't hot, but warmish because they're heated by the sun. As other reviewers have noted, they are basically two segregated swimming pools, the men's at least made of local rock. The pool is small, but looks fine, inviting even, apart from men in the pool who were clearing their nasal passages and spitting into the water. It happened regularly, and no one seemed to mind. I did, and gave it a miss.
title: More spitting

body: This is situated at Keerimalai which is about 17 KM from Jaffna town presently the road was very well done and you can reach within 30 minutes ( Jaffna KKS road) There are ample public transport available. It is very close to Kankeasathurai Railway station. Basically it is a hot spring (Luke warm water) situated very close to the Naguleswaram Temple (Hindu Shiva Temple) There are several believes and myths about this Springs Once a saint who had a Mongoose face had got his human face after having bath here and it is believed that having a bath at this place will wash all your sins off. This is situated adjoining to the sea if the climate is good you can have a sea bath also. After having bath you can go the Shiva temple.There are two wells situated next to each other and separated by a wall one for men and other foe women you have some privacy. There are changing rooms with bathing facilities provided here for a fee but those are not clean at all. Regarding the well you must be watch full because they are slippery. This is a nice place but very badly maintained. There are no entry fee. I am told it will get crowded when time goes if you want a clean and smooth bathing better you go early in the morning (like 6 am)
title: Warm water springs

body: These are two cement tanks. One for men and one for women. The water is lukewarm. The changing rooms are filthy and nightmarish. Far too many noisy kids screeching and running around in their underwear. A dip in the sea behind this spot is much more interesting. The water outlet canal from these tanks is also directed to the sea there.
title: Basically two cement tanks

body: It is well maintained by the local body. However the pool should have a shower fitted so that most bathers and douse themselves before jumping to the pool. This is important as many pilgrims arrive from distances and it would ensure considerations from a health point of view as it is a community pool.
title: Community

body: Keerimalai Shiva Temple is one of my regular visiting places whenever I travel to Jaffna.It is because as Hindus we have some duties to fulfil at this temple for our dead blood relatives.There has been tremendous improvements that have been made during the past few years.The temple refurbishment work is in progress. The road leading from maviddapuram kantha swamy kovil to keerimalai is now tarred and makes travel more comfortable.The temple itself has historical importance for Hindus which is also called Nahuleswaram. It gives you immense happiness and peace to pray at this temple.We travelled by a three wheeler to this destination from Jaffna Town.
title: NEW ROADS

body: We caught a local bus there and back from Jaffna which was half the fun. 40 minutes crammed in with locals going past markets and temples on our way. The Springs have been made into a swimming pool with a open Mens area and a walled in Womans area. It is only waist high and the bottom is large boulders with some sandy patches. It was not a hot spring but more a salt water pool at normal temperature. Don't make a sepcial visit but id you do have extra time in Jaffna and feel the need to get out of the city this will do the trick.
title: Not really hot springs, More a salt water bath

body: This is an experience that you must try when visiting Jaffna, the water coming into the springs is to this day still unknown where it comes from which is what makes it special! (Be careful when getting into the water as the rocks are slippery.)
title: A memorable experience!

body: This is a religious place and hot water springs... supposed to be with healing powers for those with belief....so it is not a touristic place
title: wrong name.. not "hot"

body: Visited the place on our way to Point Pedro. The entrance to the Women's section did not look too welcoming. In spite of instructions that soap should not be used we saw a little girl happily soaping herself - while her Mum looked on. The spelling on the Notice Board has to be rectified - re "Fealty" words.
title: Visited the place...

body: We visited Keerimalai (which apparently translates from Tamil to Mongoose Mountain according to my Dad!) early on a Sunday morning - it was baking hot so a dip in the spring was very welcomed. The area for men to bathe is very nice with a view of the sea. The area for women, whilst the water was still nice, had tall walls around it and was less scenic. We were the first women to arrive so we had the spring to ourselves! It would have been nice if we could have bathed in the men's area as well though! It was free to bathe in the pool and 20rs to use the fresh water showers. Definitely a must see of northern Sri Lanka!
title: Lovely spring and no tourists!

body: It was a fabulous experience to have a hot water bath at Keerimalai Hot Springs. There after we jumped in to keeramalai beach too. Wash room for fresh water baths available on site with excellent toilets and changing rooms.
title: Hot water for a Hot day

body: A swim in the sacred pond having healing powers... I was lucky to be one of the people who have been here, more so ever I had gone there on a weekday so there weren't many people, I really enjoyed swimming in the pond, the water too was slightly warm and felt very pure and fresh, I came out only after 1 hour, that too because I would have missed the bus back to Jaffna!!
title: A swim in the sacred pond having healing powers...

body: The waters here are said to be therapeutic. The baths are of historic and religious importance to believers. Hence a "must visit" place .This is a great place to observe social interactions and religious observances amongst the people of Jaffna and others who visit here. There are separate baths for men and women . Had I been prepared, I would have liked to try it -- shall do so on my next visit.There are special days in July and February which are considered to be auspicious for a healing dip. The baths would be particularly colorful on such occasions.
title: Healing waters

body: This spring is an excellent stop if your in Jaffna. The spring is split into male and female areas with the latter being enclosed behind a wall. For men, a dip in the male spring is a fantastic experience. The locals with no doubt have a chat with you and the water is a great temperature and the whole pool itself is in a nice setting.
title: Good for men

body: The young men and women had their own part of the building , easy access to the beach area. Interesting to mingle with the friendly locals.
title: mingling with the locals,

body: We visited during a hot day, so the cool water was appreciated.I always find these temple baths, green, slimy and floating with plastic bottles.Although it was a little bit slimy and green, it was clean and full of locals up for a chat or swimming race. The water is supposed to be spring fed, but I think there is a large content of ocean water. I'm still waiting for my religious epiphany from my dip, but it certainly cooled my body temperature. There did not appear to be change rooms, but there is a changing alcove that is respected by every bather. Ladies, you can watch, but not stare, you have your own pool. Women only, so I can't tell you any more.
title: What an amazing experience
Just another place to see!!
body: This pond is said to have medicinal/healing properties, even said to make barren women become fertile. So it is a ritual for most people who visit Jaffna. But if your just a tourist then it may not be worth the effort.It tends to get quite crowded. Separate area for women.

title: I think they fib
body: The local tour guide told us that the pool was fresh water, but having swum there this is not the case. Once again it was not hard to pick the non local in the pool, and with 100 or so local school children watching, was entertaining. The near by temple also worth a look too.
